title: How Rho cuts escalations 3× with continuous review of human and AI agents
summary: Rho cuts customer escalations 3×, reviews 100% of conversations and lifts containment by 10 percentage points with Rulebase. See how human resolutions can drive better AI agents.

Rho spots issues as they happen, across both human and AI conversations. With[AI agent monitoring](https://rulebase.co/product/read-every-interaction) , every human resolution becomes a tested fix for the agent — lifting containment 10 points and cutting customer escalations 3×.


For the business banking platform, customer experience was a priority from the beginning. Quality assurance was already in place across phone, email and chat. The challenge was seeing enough of what customers experienced to act in time.


## Quality was in place.
Visibility was the missing piece.


Manual QA meant finding conversations, pulling them together and reviewing a small selection. That work covered only 3–5% of interactions, leaving most of the customer experience outside the review process.


For Stas Johnson-Chyzhykov, Rho’s Chief Operating Officer, the frustration was timing. The team was committed to quality, but often caught problems after they had already developed. Rho wanted to spot issues while there was still time to change the outcome.


> “But we always felt we were behind … With Rulebase, we can be forward-looking.”


## From a small sample
to every interaction.


Rulebase expanded review to 100% of Rho’s phone, email and chat conversations, evaluating them against Rho’s operating standards. Managers could see when a conversation went off track and identify patterns across the wider operation.


The broader coverage gave the team a better basis for deciding what needed coaching and what needed an operational fix. A recurring issue could be investigated as a pattern, rather than appearing as an isolated miss in a small sample.


The same review covers AI agents. Rulebase reads bot conversations against those operating standards too, and reports resolution by intent rather than as a single average, so a missed intent, an unsupported answer or a failed tool call surfaces as clearly as a human miss.


Handoffs are judged, not just counted. A request that goes to a person is checked for whether it should have escalated and whether the specialist had the context to finish it, which separates an appropriate handoff from an avoidable one.


When a bot hands a request to a person, the review follows it through to resolution. That pairing is what starts the improvement loop: the human resolution shows the step the agent was missing, which becomes a knowledge, prompt or tool change, tested against realistic scenarios before it ships and measured on the same intent afterwards.


## Less time assembling reviews.
More time going deeper.


For Jeff Pasquerella, Rho’s Head of Compliance, the difference was practical: gathering samples could previously take a week. Rulebase brought that work down to minutes, giving the team room to examine more conversations and investigate more thoroughly.


The team no longer had to be as selective about what it reviewed. That change helped surface issues that the old process would have missed.


> “Rulebase enables us to catch what sampling never could.”


## What happens after
an issue is found?


Rho’s use of Rulebase extends beyond review. Its operations team runs agents that act on the signals: a customer showing signs of risk, another contact about the same unresolved issue, or a service deadline approaching.


Those agents bring in the responsible team and follow the work through. Weekly reviews also surface product feedback and service gaps, which are routed to the people who can address them.


In July 2026, Rho and Rulebase announced a multi-year partnership, extending the relationship from conversation review into automated customer-operations workflows.


## The human resolution
is the bot’s next lesson.


A handoff tells you where the bot stopped. What the human does next can show you how to improve it. Did they find a missing policy, check a transaction, use a different tool or ask a question the bot missed?


Rulebase connects those two sides of the same customer journey. Review the failed AI interaction alongside the human resolution, identify the knowledge, prompt or tool gap, then turn the successful steps into a proposed fix. Simulate the change across realistic customer scenarios before releasing it.


Rho’s move to full conversation coverage provides the foundation for that loop: find the issue, understand how it was resolved and act on the finding. For human teams, that means focused coaching and better processes. For AI agents, it means a growing set of lessons and tests drawn from how customers actually get help.

## Learn from your best humans.
Build a better bot.


Your human agents already solve the problems your bot cannot. Rulebase brings their resolutions into the same view as AI failures, so a handoff becomes a source of learning: what was missing, what the human did differently and what the bot needs next.


Close the loop across both teams. Use conversation review to coach human agents and improve workflows. Use successful human resolutions to draft bot fixes, test them in simulation and monitor whether the next version completes more requests. Track results by intent, tool action and handoff so an average containment rate cannot hide a broken journey.

What to measure as AI coverage grows


## Better containment.
With the right handoffs preserved.


Pair containment with completed tasks, repeat contact and handoff quality. Fraud, vulnerability and other specialist cases should still reach the right person quickly.


### Resolution by intent


Track task completion and repeat contact for each workflow. See where the next improvement will matter most.


### Avoidable handoffs


Separate missing-knowledge and tool-failure transfers from cases that need a human decision.


### Time from failure to tested fix


Measure how long it takes to detect a recurring issue, diagnose it and validate a proposed change.


### Regressions before release


Compare agent versions on the same scenarios. Check task completion, tool state and safe escalation paths.


A measurement framework for AI operations. These are not additional quantified Rho results.


The monitoring and simulation loop


## From a human resolution
to a better AI release.


A training gym built from real customer work. Monitor human and AI conversations, trace failed intents through the human handoff and turn the resolution into a fix. Then simulate the journey to check that the bot can complete it next time.


For a refund, did the agent verify the transaction before answering? For card replacement, do later tool results reflect the updated card state? Test the full journey, including timeouts and specialist handoffs. Compare versions before release, then check live outcomes after the change.

## A closer look


Does Rulebase cover human and AI agents? +


Yes. Rulebase evaluates both against your standards and follows the customer outcome across handoffs. Findings can lead to human coaching, AI prompt or knowledge changes, and workflow improvements.


How do simulations help improve an AI agent? +


Failed conversations become test scenarios. Compare an existing agent with a proposed version across confusing requests, tool errors and difficult handoffs. Check task completion, answer accuracy and regressions before releasing a change.


What should you measure beyond containment? +


Check whether the request was completed, whether the customer had to come back, and whether a handoff reached the right person with the right context. A conversation staying with an AI agent does not, by itself, show that the customer’s problem was solved.
